title: Jio Platforms Files for India's Biggest IPO as Groww Profit Jumps 54%
excerpt: Jio's Rs 30,213 crore issue at Rs 1,065-1,119 a share would value the Reliance digital arm at Rs 10.3 lakh crore, while Groww's parent posts Rs 724.7 crore in Q2 profit on revenue up 47%.
body:
• Jio Platforms has filed its red herring prospectus for a Rs 30,213 crore IPO - set to be India's largest ever - at a price band of Rs 1,065-1,119, valuing the company at about Rs 10.3 lakh crore.
  • The all-fresh issue opens October 21 and closes October 23, with anchor bidding on October 19; Rs 27,500 crore of proceeds will repay borrowings.
  • Groww's parent reported Q2 FY27 net profit of Rs 724.7 crore, up 54% year on year, on revenue up 47% to Rs 1,501.5 crore, though profit slipped 1.4% sequentially.
  • Reader check: the Jio lot size is 12 shares, so a retail application at the top of the band is about Rs 13,428; eligible Reliance shareholders have a Rs 2,500 crore reservation and employees get a Rs 54 discount.

Jio Platforms, the Reliance Industries arm that houses India's largest telecom operator, has filed its red herring prospectus for a Rs 30,213 crore initial public offering, according to Inc42. At the upper end of its Rs 1,065-1,119 price band the issue would be India's biggest ever, surpassing Hyundai Motor India's Rs 27,800 crore offering in October 2024, and would value Jio Platforms at about Rs 10.3 lakh crore.

The numbers arrived in the same news cycle as a second marker of the retail-investing boom: Groww's parent, Billionbrains Garage Ventures, reported a 54% year-on-year jump in quarterly profit. Together the two stories define India's current equity moment - a mega-listing from the country's largest digital platform, and maturing profitability at its largest retail broker.

The Jio issue, in detail

The offering is entirely a fresh issue of 27 crore equity shares with a face value of Rs 10 each - there is no offer-for-sale, so existing investors including Meta (9.98%) and Google (7.73%) are not selling. Reliance Industries holds 66.43%. Of the proceeds, Rs 27,500 crore will repay borrowings and Rs 2,713 crore is earmarked for corporate purposes, growth, capital expenditure, working capital and marketing, according to the filing details reported by Hindu BusinessLine.

The pricing came in below street estimates that had pegged the raise at Rs 33,000-38,000 crore. BusinessLine noted Jio carries about Rs 27,500 crore of borrowings, and that clearing them is expected to lower annual interest costs by Rs 2,000-2,500 crore. Shares worth Rs 500 crore are reserved for eligible employees, who receive a Rs 54 per-share discount, and Rs 2,500 crore for eligible Reliance Industries shareholders. The lot size is 12 shares.

Jio enters the market profitable and growing. In Q1 FY27, operating revenue rose 11.8% year on year to Rs 39,173 crore, net profit rose 9.2% to Rs 7,764 crore and EBITDA rose 15.1% to Rs 20,865 crore, according to Inc42. For FY26 the company reported consolidated net profit of Rs 30,064 crore on revenue of Rs 1.49 lakh crore. The risks flagged in coverage are equally clear: wireless subscriber growth is plateauing, future earnings depend heavily on tariff increases that could drive churn, and satellite and infrastructure capital spending could squeeze margins.

Groww's profit run

Groww's consolidated net profit rose 54% year on year to Rs 724.7 crore in the quarter ended September 2026, from Rs 471.3 crore a year earlier, on operating revenue up 47% to Rs 1,501.5 crore. Consolidated EBITDA rose 60% to Rs 969 crore, while expenses rose 28.5% to Rs 555.9 crore. For the first half of FY27, net profit reached Rs 1,459.74 crore on revenue of Rs 3,002.95 crore, according to the results coverage in Hindu BusinessLine.

The sequential picture is flatter. Profit slipped 1.4% from Rs 735 crore in the June quarter and revenue was almost unchanged, as equity derivatives revenue fell after the introduction of the closing auction system in August. Groww said growth in margin trading and commodity derivatives offset that weakness, and it expects those lower-penetration businesses to contribute a larger share of income in coming quarters.

What happens next

Anchor investors bid for Jio shares on October 19, the public issue runs October 21-23, and the listing is expected on October 28. The issue's reception will be read as a verdict on large-cap Indian tech valuations at a moment when global fundraising has weakened but India's primary market has stayed active for a second consecutive year. For Groww, the next test is whether margin trading and commodities can keep replacing derivatives income if the closing-auction drag persists.
